import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.patches import FancyBboxPatch, FancyArrowPatch
import os

plt.rcParams.update({
    'font.family': 'DejaVu Sans',
    'font.size': 10,
    'figure.dpi': 300,
    'savefig.dpi': 300,
    'savefig.bbox': 'tight',
    'savefig.pad_inches': 0.1,
})

C_CKA  = '#009E73'
C_RAND = '#E69F00'
C_STD  = '#CC79A7'
C_RASP = '#D55E00'
C_BLUE = '#0072B2'

def light(hx, f=0.82):
    r, g, b = int(hx[1:3],16), int(hx[3:5],16), int(hx[5:7],16)
    return '#{:02x}{:02x}{:02x}'.format(int(r+(255-r)*f), int(g+(255-g)*f), int(b+(255-b)*f))

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 8))
ax.set_xlim(-0.3, 14.3)
ax.set_ylim(-0.5, 8.3)
ax.axis('off')

def rbox(x, y, w, h, ec='black', fc='white', lw=1.5, pad=0.08):
    ax.add_patch(FancyBboxPatch((x, y), w, h, boxstyle=f'round,pad={pad}',
                                facecolor=fc, edgecolor=ec, linewidth=lw, zorder=2))

def arr(x1, y1, x2, y2, color='#888', lw=1.2, ms=11):
    ax.add_patch(FancyArrowPatch((x1, y1), (x2, y2), arrowstyle='->', color=color,
                                 lw=lw, mutation_scale=ms, zorder=3))

# ── ROW 1: Pretrained LLM → Structural Analysis ──────────────
rbox(0.3, 6.55, 2.8, 1.15, ec=C_BLUE, fc=light(C_BLUE), lw=2)
ax.text(1.7, 7.28, 'Pretrained', fontsize=11, ha='center', va='center',
        fontweight='bold', color=C_BLUE)
ax.text(1.7, 6.95, 'Reasoning LLM', fontsize=10, ha='center', va='center', color=C_BLUE)

arr(3.1, 7.12, 4.15, 7.12, color=C_BLUE, lw=2, ms=14)

rbox(4.3, 6.15, 9.3, 1.55, ec='#555', fc='#FAFAFA', lw=2, pad=0.12)
ax.text(8.95, 7.4, 'Structural Analysis  (shared by all methods)', fontsize=11,
        ha='center', va='center', fontweight='bold', color='#333')

rbox(4.75, 6.35, 3.7, 0.75, ec='#bbb', fc='#FFF8F0', lw=1)
ax.text(6.6, 6.88, 'Taylor Importance', fontsize=9, ha='center', va='center', fontweight='bold')
ax.text(6.6, 6.55, r'$I(h) = |a_h \cdot \nabla_{a_h}\mathcal{L}|$', fontsize=9,
        ha='center', va='center')

rbox(8.9, 6.35, 4.2, 0.75, ec='#bbb', fc='#F0FFF8', lw=1)
ax.text(11.0, 6.88, 'CKA Overlap', fontsize=9, ha='center', va='center', fontweight='bold')
ax.text(11.0, 6.55, r'$F(h) = \mathrm{CKA}(h,\, h\!+\!1)$', fontsize=9,
        ha='center', va='center')

# ── ROW 2: 4 Scoring Criteria ────────────────────────────────
methods = [
    ('CKA-only', C_CKA,  r'Remove highest $F(h)$',
     'Preserves unique\nrepresentations', False),
    ('Random',   C_RAND, 'Uniform random',
     'No selection bias', False),
    ('Standard', C_STD,  r'Remove lowest $I(h)$',
     'Removes "unimportant"\nstructures', True),
    ('RASP',     C_RASP, r'$S = I(h)\!\cdot\!(1\!-\!F(h))^\alpha$',
     'Removes redundant\n+ unimportant', True),
]

bw, bh = 2.9, 1.65
bg = (13.0 - 4*bw) / 3
by = 3.85
xcs = []

for i, (name, col, formula, prop, warn) in enumerate(methods):
    x = 0.5 + i*(bw+bg)

    xcs.append(xc)

    rbox(x, by, bw, bh, ec=col, fc=light(col), lw=2)
    ax.text(xc, by+bh-0.28, name, fontsize=11, ha='center', va='center',
            fontweight='bold', color=col)
    ax.text(xc, by+bh-0.72, formula, fontsize=9, ha='center', va='center', color='#333')
    ax.plot([x+0.25, x+bw-0.25], [by+bh-1.0, by+bh-1.0],
            color=col, alpha=0.3, lw=0.8, zorder=3)
    ax.text(xc, by+0.35, prop, fontsize=8, ha='center', va='center',
            color='#555', style='italic')

    if warn:
        ax.text(x+bw-0.12, by+bh-0.08, r'$\triangle\!$ I(h)', fontsize=6.5,
                ha='right', va='top', color='#CC0000', fontweight='bold')

    arr(xc, 6.15, xc, by+bh+0.12, color='#aaa', lw=1.0, ms=9)

# ── Recovery Pipeline ─────────────────────────────────────────
py, ph = 2.7, 0.6
rbox(0.5, py, 13.0, ph, ec='#777', fc='#F0F0F0', lw=1.5)
ax.text(7.0, py+ph/2, 'Identical Recovery:   SFT Warmup  →  GRPO RL Alignment',
        fontsize=11, ha='center', va='center', fontweight='bold', color='#555')

for xc in xcs:
    arr(xc, by, xc, py+ph+0.1, color='#aaa', lw=1.0, ms=9)

# ── ROW 3: Divergent Outcomes ─────────────────────────────────
outcomes = [
    ('Active\nLearning',    C_CKA,  'reward 0.354',  'frac_zero 0.125', 2.5),
    ('Stagnation',          C_RAND, 'reward ≈0.17', 'flat trajectory', 1.8),
    ('Collapse',            C_STD,  'reward →0',    'grad vanishing',  1.2),
    ('Immediate\nCollapse', C_RASP, 'reward ≈0.01', '85% max-len',     0.8),

oy, oh, ow = 0.4, 1.7, bw

for i, (name, col, l1, l2, alw) in enumerate(outcomes):
    x = 0.5 + i*(ow+bg)
    xc = xcs[i]

    arr(xc, py, xc, oy+oh+0.1, color=col, lw=alw, ms=12)
    rbox(x, oy, ow, oh, ec=col, fc=light(col), lw=2)
    ax.text(xc, oy+oh-0.42, name, fontsize=10, ha='center', va='center',
            fontweight='bold', color=col)
    ax.text(xc, oy+0.52, l1, fontsize=8.5, ha='center', va='center',
            color='#444', family='monospace')
    ax.text(xc, oy+0.22, l2, fontsize=8, ha='center', va='center',
            color='#666', family='monospace')

# ── Recovery Capacity Gradient (horizontal bar below outcomes) ─
import numpy as np

grad_y = 0.0

cmap = LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list('rc', [C_CKA, C_RAND, C_STD, C_RASP])
ax.imshow(grad_img, aspect='auto', cmap=cmap, alpha=0.7,
          extent=[x_left, x_right, grad_y - grad_h, grad_y + grad_h], zorder=2)
ax.text((x_left+x_right)/2, grad_y - 0.28, 'Recovery Capacity',
        fontsize=9, ha='center', va='top', color='#444', fontweight='bold')
ax.text(x_left - 0.1, grad_y, 'High', fontsize=8, ha='right', va='center',
        color=C_CKA, fontweight='bold')
ax.text(x_right + 0.1, grad_y, 'None', fontsize=8, ha='left', va='center',
        color=C_RASP, fontweight='bold')

plt.tight_layout()

outdir = '/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_17/projects/recovery_aware_struct_prune/artifacts/figures'
fig.savefig(f'{outdir}/fig1_framework.pdf')
fig.savefig(f'{outdir}/fig1_framework.png')

for ext in ['pdf', 'png']:
    p = f'{outdir}/fig1_framework.{ext}'

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate CKA paper figures from pre-extracted JSON data."""

import json
import numpy as np
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from pathlib import Path

plt.rcParams.update({
    "font.family": "serif",
    "font.size": 12,
    "axes.labelsize": 13,
    "axes.titlesize": 13,
    "xtick.labelsize": 10,
    "ytick.labelsize": 10,
    "figure.dpi": 150,
    "savefig.dpi": 300,
    "savefig.bbox": "tight",
    "savefig.pad_inches": 0.05,
})

RESULTS_DIR = Path("/root/recovery_aware_struct_prune/results")
FIG_DIR = RESULTS_DIR / "figures"
FIG_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)


def load_data():
    with open(RESULTS_DIR / "cka_per_layer.json") as f:
        per_layer = json.load(f)["per_layer"]
    with open(RESULTS_DIR / "cka_heatmap.json") as f:
        heatmap = json.load(f)
    return per_layer, heatmap


def plot_per_layer_overlap(per_layer):
    """Fig A: Per-layer mean CKA overlap - grouped bars for Attention vs MLP."""
    layers = sorted(int(k) for k in per_layer.keys())
    attn_means = [per_layer[str(i)]["attn_mean"] for i in layers]
    mlp_means = [per_layer[str(i)]["mlp_mean"] for i in layers]

    x = np.arange(len(layers))
    w = 0.38

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 3))
    bars_attn = ax.bar(x - w / 2, attn_means, w, label="Attention heads",
                       color="#4C72B0", edgecolor="white", linewidth=0.3)
    bars_mlp = ax.bar(x + w / 2, mlp_means, w, label="MLP neurons",
                      color="#DD8452", edgecolor="white", linewidth=0.3)

    # Annotate top-3 overlap layers (by combined mean)
    combined = [(attn_means[i] + mlp_means[i], i) for i in range(len(layers))]
    combined.sort(reverse=True)
    for _, idx in combined[:3]:
        y_top = max(attn_means[idx], mlp_means[idx])
        ax.plot(idx, y_top + 0.015, marker="v", markersize=7,
                color="#C44E52", clip_on=False)

    ax.set_xlabel("Layer index")
    ax.set_ylabel("Mean $\\mathcal{F}(h)$")
    ax.set_xticks(x[::2])
    ax.set_xticklabels([str(i) for i in layers[::2]])
    ax.set_ylim(0.4, 1.05)
    ax.legend(frameon=True, fontsize=10, loc="lower right",
              framealpha=0.9, edgecolor="0.8")
    ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)
    ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.3, linewidth=0.5)

    out = FIG_DIR / "cka_per_layer_overlap.pdf"
    fig.savefig(out)
    plt.close(fig)
    print(f"Saved {out}")
    return attn_means, mlp_means, layers


def plot_cka_heatmaps(heatmap, attn_means, mlp_means, layers):
    """Fig B: CKA similarity heatmaps for highest- and lowest-overlap layers."""
    combined = [attn_means[i] + mlp_means[i] for i in range(len(layers))]
    hi_layer = layers[int(np.argmax(combined))]
    lo_layer = layers[int(np.argmin(combined))]

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(7.5, 6.5),
                             gridspec_kw={"hspace": 0.35, "wspace": 0.30})

    pairs = [(hi_layer, "High-overlap"), (lo_layer, "Low-overlap")]
    for col, (layer_idx, label) in enumerate(pairs):
        layer_data = heatmap[str(layer_idx)]
        attn_mat = np.array(layer_data["attn_cka_matrix"])
        mlp_mat = np.array(layer_data["mlp_cka_matrix"])

        # Attention heatmap
        ax = axes[0, col]
        im = ax.imshow(attn_mat, cmap="coolwarm", vmin=0.0, vmax=1.0, aspect="equal")
        ax.set_xlabel("Head index")
        ax.set_ylabel("Head index")
        ax.set_xticks(range(attn_mat.shape[0]))
        ax.set_yticks(range(attn_mat.shape[0]))
        ax.set_title(f"{label} layer {layer_idx} -- Attn", fontsize=11)
        for i in range(attn_mat.shape[0]):
            for j in range(attn_mat.shape[1]):
                ax.text(j, i, f"{attn_mat[i, j]:.2f}", ha="center", va="center",
                        fontsize=7.5, color="white" if attn_mat[i, j] < 0.5 else "black")

        # MLP heatmap (subsample if large)
        ax2 = axes[1, col]
        if mlp_mat.shape[0] > 16:
            step = mlp_mat.shape[0] // 14
            idx = list(range(0, mlp_mat.shape[0], step))
            mlp_sub = mlp_mat[np.ix_(idx, idx)]
            tick_labels = [str(i) for i in idx]
        else:
            mlp_sub = mlp_mat
            tick_labels = [str(i) for i in range(mlp_mat.shape[0])]

        im2 = ax2.imshow(mlp_sub, cmap="viridis", vmin=np.min(mlp_sub) * 0.98,
                         vmax=1.0, aspect="equal")
        ax2.set_xlabel("Neuron group")
        ax2.set_ylabel("Neuron group")
        ax2.set_xticks(range(len(tick_labels)))
        ax2.set_xticklabels(tick_labels, fontsize=7)
        ax2.set_yticks(range(len(tick_labels)))
        ax2.set_yticklabels(tick_labels, fontsize=7)
        ax2.set_title(f"{label} layer {layer_idx} -- MLP", fontsize=11)
        plt.colorbar(im2, ax=ax2, fraction=0.046, pad=0.04)

    # Shared colorbar for attention row
    plt.colorbar(im, ax=axes[0, :].tolist(), fraction=0.02, pad=0.04, label="CKA")

    out = FIG_DIR / "cka_heatmap.pdf"
    fig.savefig(out)
    plt.close(fig)
    print(f"Saved {out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    per_layer, heatmap = load_data()
    attn_means, mlp_means, layers = plot_per_layer_overlap(per_layer)
    plot_cka_heatmaps(heatmap, attn_means, mlp_means, layers)
    print("Done.")

1	\section{Introduction}
2	\label{sec:intro}
3	
4	Reasoning Large Language Models can be compressed through structured pruning, but the pruned model must recover its reasoning capabilities through fine-tuning.
5	The dominant assumption is that the recovery paradigm (SFT versus RLVR) determines recovery quality: \citet{selfhealing2025} demonstrate that RLVR restores pruned reasoning models to near-original accuracy, significantly outperforming SFT.
6	We show that this hierarchy is an artifact of suboptimal pruning.
7	When pruning preserves representational diversity, recovery method choice becomes irrelevant: at 20\% sparsity, mean $|\Delta(\text{GRPO}-\text{SFT})| {=} 0.54$\,pp across the four fine-grained criteria (max $0.61$\,pp); including dose-response variations and MBPP, the maximum is $1.34$\,pp.
8	What matters is not \emph{how} you train after pruning, but \emph{which structures} you remove.
9	
10	This gap is surprising because RL and SFT impose fundamentally different demands on model representations: RL compresses incorrect paths while SFT expands correct ones~\citep{rlsqueezes2026}. Yet existing structured pruning methods for reasoning LLMs~\citep{graspprune2026,resp2025,llmpruner2023,bonsai2025} optimize for post-pruning quality without studying how the criterion shapes downstream RL recovery.
11	No prior work has compared multiple pruning criteria under RL or asked whether the ``RLVR $>$ SFT'' advantage persists across pruning strategies.
12	We note that \citet{selfhealing2025} evaluate unstructured magnitude pruning retaining 96.5\% of dense parameters; our findings concern fine-grained structural pruning where entire channel groups are removed, and the two settings may impose different demands on RL recovery.
13	
14	\begin{figure}[t]
15	\centering
16	\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{../figures/paper/fig1_dose_response.pdf}
17	\caption{Dose-response curve for the CKA diversity coefficient $\alpha$ at 20\% MLP channel sparsity on GSM8K ($N{=}1{,}319$). Recovery accuracy follows an inverted-U, peaking at $\alpha{=}2.0$ (66.11\%). SFT and GRPO curves nearly overlap ($|\Delta| \leq 1.14$\,pp at every point), visually demonstrating reward-accuracy decoupling: the pruning criterion, not the recovery paradigm, determines outcome.}
18	\label{fig:dose_response}
19	\end{figure}
20	
21	We present a controlled comparison on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B~\citep{deepseek2025r1} at 20\% MLP channel sparsity, varying the balance between gradient importance and CKA-based representational diversity~\citep{kornblith2019cka} via a coefficient $\alpha$ in the pruning score (Figure~\ref{fig:dose_response}).
22	The dose-response curve reveals an inverted-U: recovery peaks at $\alpha{=}2.0$ (66.11\% GRPO on GSM8K~\citep{cobbe2021gsm8k}), where importance and diversity reach optimal balance.
23	Under GRPO~\citep{shao2024grpo} training, four criteria produce a \textbf{recovery capacity spectrum}---from active learning (CKA-only, peak reward 4.4$\times$ Standard) through stagnation (Random) to collapse ($\alpha{=}1.0$)---that tracks preserved representational diversity, not gradient importance.
24	A depth pruning baseline (ShortGPT;~\citealp{shortgpt2024}) is the only method with $|\Delta| > 1$\,pp on GSM8K ($-$1.36\,pp), confirming that pruning granularity interacts with RL trainability.
25	
26	Our contributions are:
27	\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
28	    \item \textbf{Reward-accuracy decoupling.} At 20--25\% sparsity, GRPO and SFT produce near-identical accuracy across all four fine-grained criteria: mean $|\Delta| {=} 0.54$\,pp at 20\% (max $0.61$\,pp; $1.34$\,pp including dose-response variations and MBPP). At 15\%, GRPO can still amplify the CKA-guided advantage ($+$1.51\,pp differential), but this partial exception reinforces the main pattern: the pruning criterion, not the recovery paradigm, determines outcome (\S\ref{sec:decoupling}).
29	    \item \textbf{Recovery capacity spectrum.} We propose \rasp{}, which balances gradient importance with CKA-based representational diversity via a coefficient $\alpha$. A dose-response analysis on GSM8K reveals an inverted-U peaking at $\alpha{=}2.0$ (66.11\%). Under GRPO training, four criteria produce qualitatively distinct dynamics---from active learning to full collapse---that track preserved diversity, not gradient importance. The spectrum is validated across scales (1.5B) and, via SFT-based recovery, across architectures (Qwen2.5-Math-7B) (\S\ref{sec:scoring}, \S\ref{sec:recovery_gradient}, \S\ref{sec:extended_analysis}).
30	\end{enumerate}
